html:
La Matanza, the Massacre, was the killing of thousands of peasants, most of them Indigenous Pipil, by the army of El Salvador in January and February 1932, after a failed rising.

Coffee prices had collapsed in the Great Depression, wages were cut, and in December 1931 General Maximiliano Hernández Martínez seized power. On 22 January 1932 peasants in the western coffee country rose with machetes, led partly by communists under Farabundo Martí. They killed fewer than a hundred people.

The army and landowners' militias then killed somewhere between 10,000 and 40,000 people, often anyone who looked Indigenous. The Pipil stopped speaking Nawat and wearing their dress in public out of fear. The massacre began fifty years of army rule in El Salvador, and its memory fed the civil war.
sum: La Matanza, the Massacre, was the killing of thousands of peasants, most of them Indigenous Pipil, by the army of El Salvador in January and February 1932, after a failed rising.
